'Eight times across five verses' is unsupported on any scope I can recover.

findings.exactExcerpt: The Greek New Testament has a striking phrase that appears nine times in the Pastoral Epistles (1 Timothy, 2 Timothy, Titus) and almost nowhere else. The phrase is *hygiainousa didaskalia* — *sound* or *healthy doctrine*. The Greek adjective *hygiainō* is the standard medical term
findings.problem: Two problems in the hook. (1) The exact phrase *hygiainousa didaskalia* occurs four times (1 Timothy 1:10; 2 Timothy 4:3; Titus 1:9; 2:1); the verb ὑγιαίνω occurs eight times in the Pastorals in various collocations (also 'sound words', 'sound in faith'). 'Nine times' matches neither the phrase nor the word family, and the scope (phrase vs. verb) is not stated. (2) ὑγιαίνω is a verb, not 'the Greek adjective'; *hygiainousa* is its present participle.

localEvidence.observation: Occurrences of ὑγιαίνω in the Pastorals: 1 Tim 1:10; 6:3; 2 Tim 1:13; 4:3; Tit 1:9; 1:13; 2:1; 2:2 (eight). Exact 'sound doctrine' collocation: four.

findings.claimScope: Lemma ὑγιαίνω vs. the collocation 'sound doctrine'; Pastoral Epistles; Nestle 1904 / RP2018 agree.
findings.plausibleAlternative: Nine may have been reached by adding the adjective ὑγιής at Titus 2:8 ('sound message') to the eight verb occurrences — which would make the claim about the word family, not the phrase.
findings.suggestedMinimalCorrection: '…a striking expression that recurs through the Pastoral Epistles — four times as “sound doctrine,” and eight times in all for the verb *hygiainō* — and almost nowhere else. … The Greek verb *hygiainō* …'

findings.exactExcerpt: This is the more common verb in the New Testament for "to die" or "to be dying." Used hundreds of times in the gospels, Acts, and the epistles.
findings.problem: ἀποθνῄσκω occurs 111 times in the New Testament (Nestle/NA agree within one), i.e., about a hundred, not 'hundreds'. The neighbouring claim about θνῄσκω that 'most appearances are in the perfect tense (*tethnēka*) or the present participle (*thnēskontes*)' is also doubtful: the New Testament's nine occurrences of θνῄσκω are all perfect forms; no present participle of the simple verb occurs.

localEvidence.observation: Article line 24 ff.; counts from the Nestle 1904 lemma index would settle both claims.

findings.claimScope: Lemmata ἀποθνῄσκω and θνῄσκω; New Testament; Nestle 1904.
findings.suggestedMinimalCorrection: 'Used over a hundred times…' and 'all of its New Testament appearances are perfect forms (*tethnēken*, “has died”)'.

findings.exactExcerpt: The Sunday school teacher angle is direct: teach the etymology of *hypakoē* and what it reveals about Christian obedience.

findings.exactExcerpt: The Formula of Concord Article VIII develops this at length, distinguishing three modes of the *communicatio idiomatum* — the *genus idiomaticum*, the *genus apotelesmaticum*, and the *genus maiestaticum*.

Harmless if the YAML parser drops comments, but it is a template artifact that misnames the record it sits in.

localEvidence.observation: grep -l '^# Front matter reconciled' corpora/om-articles/*.md → 14 files.

findings.suggestedMinimalCorrection: Remove the comment line from the frontmatter of the 14 files.
findings.notes: Reported once here; the other affected records are listed in COVERAGE.json with this finding id.

findings.exactExcerpt: Notice how the two publishers describe it.
findings.problem: BSB and MSB are described as 'the two publishers' / 'both publishers' in candidates 02, 03 and 21 ('Neither publisher offers a cross-reference'), but as 'both Berean editions' / 'both Berean footnotes' (one publishing programme) in candidates 05, 06, 09, 10, 12, 14, 15, 22, 26, 29, 30. The collection should decide whether the Berean Standard Bible and the Majority Standard Bible are one publisher or two and say so consistently.

localEvidence.observation: Text search across corpora/comparison-commentaries for 'two publishers', 'both publishers', 'Neither publisher' vs. 'both Berean'.

findings.claimScope: Publisher identity of BSB and MSB.
findings.suggestedMinimalCorrection: Use one formulation (e.g., 'the two Berean editions') throughout.
